title: SDK transport playbook: adaptive leases, connection priming, and graceful stream ergonomics
creator: Keiko Tanaka
description:
Background: Engineering teams building with Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) report subtle production issues in mixed-latency workloads: idle socket exhaustion during bursty traffic, opaque per-route tail latency spikes, and fragile streaming reconnect behavior when upstream transient errors occur. Existing docs cover timeouts and keepalive heuristics in fragments; this ticket creates a single cross-SDK playbook that engineers can follow and ship as default SDK presets and examples.

Goals:
- Define per-route adaptive deadline profiles and connection lease semantics for client SDKs that balance latency SLOs and connection reuse.
- Provide concrete, language-specific examples for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC transports (Python requests/urllib3, node-fetch/undici, golang net/http and grpc).
- Document connection priming (TCP+TLS warmup, HTTP/2 PING/SETTINGS priming) and socket rotation recipes to avoid head-of-line blocking and stale TLS sessions.
- Clarify streaming ergonomics: resume/backoff patterns, partial-response errors, safe retry windows, and consumer-level backpressure examples.
- Create observability hooks: metrics to surface lease contention, idle-socket churn, and per-route deadline misses.

Proposal (high level):
1) Adaptive per-route deadlines: attach three named profiles to client routes (fast, steady, bulk). Each profile contains: nominal deadline, hedging window (for optional parallel hedging), and slow-path fallback. Example defaults: fast=500ms nominal, 120ms hedging; steady=1500ms nominal; bulk=10s nominal. SDKs expose a RouteProfile enum and allow override per request.

2) Connection leases and priming: implement short-lived connection leases (lease TTL) coupled with soft-idle thresholds. A lease is a token allowing up to N requests over M seconds before proactively rotating the socket. Default heuristics: max_requests_per_lease=1000 or lease_ttl=600s, soft_idle_reap=120s. When an application starts, SDKs perform optional connection priming: single short HEAD/OPTIONS warmup or an HTTP/2 SETTINGS exchange and 1-2 PINGs. Priming should be opt-in or enabled for 'fast' profile.

3) Keepalive & pool sizing: recommend sensible defaults per language (examples below) and expose a single unified config surface: connection_pool_size, max_idle_connections, keepalive_interval, keepalive_timeout, idle_rotation_ttl. Provide platform-specific knobs (HTTP/2 concurrent streams, gRPC keepalive time/timeout).

4) Streaming ergonomics: for server-stream or chunked responses, provide a streaming helper that: a) detects transient EOF vs application-level error, b) surfaces resume tokens when available, c) supports client-level semantic retry by replaying the last acked prefix (where model APIs support token-level resumes), and d) provides exponential backoff with jitter for reconnects. For SDKs where resume tokens are impossible, document safe circuit-breaker thresholds and graceful fallbacks to batch mode.

5) Observability: emit per-request metadata: route_profile, lease_id, lease_age_seconds, pooled_connection_hit=true/false, socket_rotation_reason, request_timing_buckets. Add a small set of metrics and logs to make regressions visible in Console.

Language-specific examples (short extracts):
- Python (requests + urllib3 adapter):
  - set pool_maxsize=50, pool_block=true, keepalive_timeout=75s, socket_opts TCP_KEEPIDLE=60, TCP_KEEPINTVL=10.
  - connection priming: Session().head(url, timeout=1.0) on client startup for 'fast' routes.

- TypeScript (undici / fetch):
  - use undici.Agent with connections=40, pipelining=0 for HTTP/1.1 or keepAliveTimeout=75 for HTTP/2 Agent; set request timeout via AbortController with per-route profile values.
  - for fetch streaming, wrap body.getReader() with a resilientReader that will attempt N reconnects when Content-Length absent and upstream resets occur.

- Go (net/http + grpc):
  - http.Transport: MaxIdleConns=200, IdleConnTimeout=90s, TLSHandshakeTimeout=10s, ExpectContinueTimeout=1s.
  - gRPC: keepalive.ClientParameters{Time:60s, Timeout:20s, PermitWithoutStream:true}.
  - connection lease implemented at client wrapper: rotate net.Conn after lease_ttl or max_requests hit.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (python, ts, go) have a new config surface RouteProfile + connectionLease config and corresponding unit/integration tests.
- Default presets checked in and documented in the SDK READMEs with language examples.
- Console receives at least three new telemetry signals (lease_age_seconds, lease_rotation_count, route_profile_deadline_misses) and dashboard prototype linked in ticket.
- Performance verification: under mixed-latency synthetic workload, per-request p95 latency for 'fast' routes should not regress >5% vs baseline while reducing idle-socket churn by >=30%.

Implementation tasks:
- [ ] RFC doc describing profiles and heuristics (Confluence)
- [ ] SDK API changes and default presets (python, ts, go)
- [ ] Unit tests for lease rotation, priming, and streaming helper behavior
- [ ] Integration test harness simulating bursty traffic and connection churn
- [ ] Telemetry plumbing and Console dashboard stub
- [ ] Docs and examples for customers + migration notes

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Lease rotation increases TLS handshake overhead if leases are too short; balance by adaptive TTL that increases under steady load.
- Hedging can reduce tail latency but increases load/cost; opt-in per-route and limited to 'fast' profile by default.
- Resume semantics require server support; where unavailable, prefer client-side transparent partial-retry only for idempotent request patterns.

Security considerations:
- No secret/material changes. Ensure priming requests do not leak PII or increase audit surface; mark priming requests with a low-privilege header and avoid sending payload bodies.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence RFC (WIP): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SDK-Transport-Playbook
- Integration test harness repo (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-transport-harness/pull/12
- Design notes (Console dashboard mock): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/sdk-telemetry-mock

Rollout plan:
1) Land RFC and critical unit tests (week 1).
2) Ship SDK defaults behind a feature flag across languages (week 2).
3) Enable telemetry and collect 2 weeks of data with internal canary orgs.
4) Flip feature flag once thresholds met and publish migration guide.
comments: 2026-03-10 Keiko Tanaka: Created initial ticket and high-level proposal. Asked SDK leads for feasibility notes.

2026-03-11 Marcela Gomez (SDK lead - TS): Reviewed. Suggested changing default undici connections from 40->30 for node12 worker cost constraints. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/458
2026-03-11 Ravi Shah: Prototype for Python lease rotation implemented; observed TLS handshake increase ~12% when lease_ttl < 60s. Will tune with adaptive backoff.
2026-03-12 UX review: added note to surface route_profile in SDK debug logs. Example log format included in RFC.
2026-03-12 SRE: requested retention for telemetry metrics >=90 days for trend analysis.
notes: Avoids making priming the default for low-traffic SDK consumers unless route profile set to 'fast'. Will add opt-out env var REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_PRIMING=true for private deploys.
